title: Review of c40's layered CIPS division (C:metabolic-cell, SIBED): replicates on fresh seed 4 (3 founders, 8 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 merges by t=12000; layer on 100% of body-frames; fuel fork at t=8000 dissolves all 13 bodies within 200 t, also with turnover off); with the amphiphile made only on body pixels the layer is unchanged, so B is self-made, not by construction
summary: Re-ran c40's world.py unchanged on unused seed 4 (labkit, 192^2, T=12000) and c40's fork.py on seed 4 (fork at t=8000, arms fed / kF=0 / kF=0 with d=0). Pack: 3 condensates nucleate from the random field, grow, elongate and pinch; 11 splits, 8 persistent, generation 2, 0 merges, 14 bodies at the end. layer_share.py (signed distance to the e=0.5 contour, every 10th frame): every body passes rim/core and rim/out >= 1.5 at every sampled time (median rim/core 4.9-7.6, rim/out 24-27). Code read: the amphiphile s is made by catalysis everywhere and adsorbs by a drift written against the enzyme field; on my seed the bodies make only 26-48% of the catalysis (the s source) until t~4500, rising to 79% by t=11600, so the bath makes most of it early. Deciding control (world_bodysrc.py, body_src=1: s made only where e > 0.5, same bodies): the layer is unchanged (100% pass, rim/core 4.6-7.2, rim/out 27-30), so the bodies' own production suffices. Fork: fed twin 13 -> 12 bodies; kF=0 and kF=0+d=0 both 13 -> 0 by t=8200 (fork_s4.png).

verdicts.limitation: Pack to T=12000 only (generation 2). Division axes are locked to one grid diagonal; my finding 20261026T1158-c39-cips-division-isotropy shows division survives an isotropic drift flux in the unlayered parent world, not re-checked with the layer. The fork removes fuel everywhere (bath catalysis also consumes it), so it shows dependence on fuel, not each body's own uptake. Growth matter comes from a uniform enzyme turnover feed. The layer does no work (s acts back on nothing). One fresh seed.
